title: Development and validation of a challenge model using geosmin‐spiked feeds to obtain off‐flavor compounds in tissues of Atlantic salmon, Salmo salar
content:
Abstract

Fish produced within recirculating aquaculture systems may develop flavors not desired by end-consumers, hereafter “off-flavor,” which is largely attributed to geosmin accumulation in fish tissues. To develop methods for mitigating geosmin accumulation, a reliable and reproducible method of introducing geosmin in fish tissue is needed. Current methods of obtaining geosmin in fish tissues typically rely on dosing via water-borne geosmin, which can be problematic due to (1) the high cost of scientific-grade geosmin and (2) complications associated with geosmin interactions with life support systems. The objectives of this research were to (1) develop an open method for producing geosmin-spiked feeds, (2) validate the use of spiked feeds as a means of dosing geosmin into Atlantic salmon, Salmo salar, tissues and (3) evaluate the relationship between geosmin concentrations measured in blood and various tissues. Five experimental geosmin-spiked feeds (10, 50, 100, 250, and 500 μg kg−1) were produced to use in a 3-week feeding trial to evaluate geosmin concentrations in juvenile salmon blood and various tissues. Benchtop trials compared geosmin losses between oil- and non-oil-coated feeds exposed to water (leaching) as well as determining storage feasibility. Leaching trial showed non-oil-coated feeds released lower quantities of geosmin (3.2% ± 0.5% loss) in surrounding water when compared to the oil-coated feed (10.4% ± 0.1% loss). Geosmin measured in feeds with increasing quantities of geosmin were not affected by storage (regression analysis, p = 0.5691). Overall, the 3-week feeding trial showed increasing concentrations of geosmin-spiked feeds linearly correlated to geosmin concentrations in muscle tissue (R 2 = 0.536), blood (R 2 = 0.549), and liver (R 2 = 0.441) of Atlantic salmon. In addition, there was a strong linear correlation between blood and muscle tissue geosmin concentrations (R 2 = 0.892). This research resulted in the establishment of an alternative dosing method for future off-flavor studies focused on Atlantic salmon and provides evidence that blood samples may be used as a proxy in providing a non-lethal means of assessing off-flavor in Atlantic salmon.
